evidence: The chain is real: freeze-suite's planJobs only queues cases with completed < level, so '-n <min>' plans nothing and buildBaseline keeps throwing 'needs one common N'. Resuming at the max instead levels the root upward (agent showed planJobs at a=2,b=1 goes from [] to [{b,2}]) and keeps paid replays, which beats the reviewer's trim-scoring cure.
guidance_note: When a comment states an invariant like 'an uneven root resumes level', trace the consumer (planJobs) to confirm the chosen end of the range actually delivers it before shipping.

evidence: foldSpend threw on bases.length > 1 while src/usage.js sumCost is documented as the one place the never-add-across-bases rule lives and resolves mixes to unpriced; an unpriced+subscription mix from one engine is reachable and the throw discarded an already-decided verdict. Agent did both reviewer cures (withhold unpriced, delegate to sumCost).
guidance_note: Before writing a fold over a tagged-currency record, grep for the existing summer of that type and call it instead of re-deriving its mixing rule.

evidence: Same defect as F2 from the call-site angle: readCandidateSpend runs while assembling the record after spend, and a throw there exits 2 with no verdict. Fixed by the same 4d0d7c1 change.
guidance_note: A secondary metric computed after the primary verdict must degrade to a typed unknown, never throw past the verdict write.

evidence: elapsedMs is Date.now()-startedMs (invocation) while waves come from readSuiteTiming over every leg under the root, so --reuse-candidate pairs ~0s with prior waves. The wall-clock line was in the PR before review (round-0 hunk); agent kept both scopes, marking legs thisInvocation by snapshot index, and justified declining the root-wide elapsed option because the budget is invocation-scoped.
guidance_note: When one sentence prints two quantities, check both come from the same scope (invocation vs. persisted root) before rendering them together.

evidence: Agent concedes 'Delegating to sumCost correctly adopted its stricter rule ... one unreported run now reaches the state. The contradiction pre-existed my change; my change made it ordinary' — and the F2 fix also edited this very Spend ternary without giving subscription+null its own arm.
guidance_note: When adopting another module's fold semantics, enumerate its output states (COST_PHRASE already listed subscription-without-notional) and give every renderer of that output an arm per state in the same commit.

evidence: A wave whose replay overruns jobTimeout makes freeze-suite exit 1, runCli throws, and main exits 2 with no verdict despite completed waves. jobTimeoutMinutes was in the pre-review PR (f1ee5ca, visible in round-0 hunk). Agent correctly showed exit codes cannot separate shortfall from crash and made the stop reason a value instead.
guidance_note: When adding a deadline that kills child work, trace what the parent does with the resulting non-zero exit and make the 'stopped short' outcome a reported verdict state in the same change.

evidence: runCli passed no timeout to the score spawn and score.js's judge fetch has no AbortSignal, contradicting the header's 'wall clock is BOUNDED'. The unbounded scoring step predates review (original PR), so not fix-caused; agent bounded it at budgetMs rather than remaining budget to avoid killing paid-for scoring, and stated the loose bound honestly.
guidance_note: When a module header claims a bound, list every blocking spawn and network call inside the bounded loop and attach a deadline to each, not just the most expensive one.

evidence: The F6 fix added 'if (assessment === undefined) throw e' with the comment 'Nothing has been measured yet'; on a resumed --out the first wave of this process has no in-memory assessment though on-disk summaries are assessable. Agent concedes it 'conflates this invocation has not assessed with nothing is assessable' and adds an assess() fallback.
guidance_note: When a fix keys behavior on in-process state, check whether the same process can start mid-history (a resumed root) where that state is empty but the persisted state is not.

evidence: The line prints 'Budget ... for this invocation' then 'perWaveUsd * repeats' for the whole ladder; on a resumed root that overstates this invocation's exposure. Agent itself calls it 'the same defect as the wall-clock line two threads over' — the invocation-vs-root scope mix fixed in F4 but not swept to the pre-spend guardrail.
guidance_note: After fixing an invocation-vs-root scope mix in one printed line, grep every other line that prints budget, cost or elapsed for the same mix before pushing.

evidence: The doc comment described fullRuns as a fractional deficit while the sole call site passes a literal 1 (already so in the round-0 hunk); the ladder redesign that orphaned it was pre-review, so not fix-caused. Agent shortened the comment and renamed the test carrying the dead convention.
guidance_note: When replacing a calling convention (deficit costing to per-wave), grep the callee's doc comment and test names for the old convention in the same commit.

narrative: A large ladder-gate PR where each round mixed genuinely pre-existing gaps (F4, F6, F7, F10) with fallout from earlier fixes. The F2 delegation to sumCost made a renderer contradiction ordinary (F5), the F6 waveFailed catch used in-process state that is empty on resume (F8), and the F4 scope fix was not swept to the cost guardrail (F9). Because each later round also held a pre-existing finding, no round was purely avoidable. Agent replies were strong: verified reachability, declined weaker cures with reasons, and owned its own regressions.
guidance_observations: The agent repeatedly diagnosed a defect class in its own reply (scope mix, late secondary step discarding a verdict) but did not sweep the rest of the file for that class before pushing; the next round found the siblings.
Fixes in eval/compare.js main() were verified by reading only, as the agent admitted for the try/catch, which is where F8's resumed-root gap slipped through.

evidence: parseBaseline did not read effort back and compareVerdict had no arm check, so a PR moving DEFAULT_SWEEP_CAP would gate across arms. Agent admits it had deferred this in the PR body and that the invariant relied on compare.js never forwarding --sweep-cap.
guidance_note: When adding a new pin to a producer artifact, trace it through every consumer of that artifact (loader and gate) in the same PR instead of deferring the last hop.

evidence: Duplicate of F1 on the same line; same 8facb31 fix covers it, with a test asserting the DEFAULT_SWEEP_CAP-move case is refused.
The meta.json, scorecard and baseline.json field lists omitted effort while all three artifacts carry it; the 8facb31 README diff adds effort to each.
guidance_note: When a new field lands on an artifact, grep the README for every enumeration of that artifact's fields and update them in the same commit.

evidence: 8facb31 added the arm check only inside compareVerdict, which runs after the full replay and scoring, while guard 4c already existed for engine drift precisely to refuse pre-spend. The 7bf6d4e diff adds the mirroring guard 4d, and the agent justified refusing rather than forcing the arm.
guidance_note: When adding a check that mirrors an existing pin (engine), mirror every enforcement point that pin has, including the pre-spend guard, not just the final comparator.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: 8facb31 touched README, baseline.js, compare.js and a test, not freeze-suite.js; the duplicated parseIntAtLeast predates review. Duplication was real, but the claimed behavioral drift via the typeof clause was not (String(n).trim() is never empty), as the agent showed; the agent moved the rule to a new eval/cli-int.js rather than score.js to keep load purity.
guidance_note: When writing a helper whose comment says 'one rule', grep sibling CLIs for the same function name before adding a second copy.

evidence: Same duplication as F5; the reviewer's cure rested on a false fact ('already exported there') — the agent quoted run-case.js's export list lacking parseIntAtLeast — and importing run-case at load would break freeze-suite's lazy-require purity. Flag false positive as for F5: 8facb31 did not touch freeze-suite.js.

The F1 and F4 fixes (8facb31, 7bf6d4e) added compareVerdict's arm refusal and guard 4d, but the 'Varying a lever' section still ended at baseline.js and 'Comparing a candidate' listed only N and engine. ff57017 adds the compare paragraph.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a new refusal to a CLI, update the README section that walks that rule's layers and the CLI's own header and USAGE in the same commit.

evidence: Guard 4d from the F4 fix was not reflected in compare.js's module header ('N and the engine are DERIVED FROM the baseline') or USAGE; ff57017 updates both.
guidance_note: Same move as F7: a new refusal path ships with its header/USAGE line.

evidence: Guard 4d checks the tree's default arm but not prior runs under a resumed --out, which carry the candidate's identity so foreignRuns passes them; readPriorRuns discarded meta.effort. Agent compared against the invocation's own arm instead of baseline.effort, correctly noting the committed baselines have a null arm so the reviewer's version would skip.
guidance_note: When adding a pre-spend pin check, ask which inputs bypass it: persisted prior runs pooled with new ones need the same check as the fresh replay.

evidence: The ff57017 README diff wrote 'N, the engine, and the effort arm come from the baseline', contradicting the paragraph it added two sections up ('refuses rather than replaying ... at the baseline's arm'). Agent: 'this one is mine from the last round'.
guidance_note: When patching an enumeration to add an item, re-read the sentence's verb against how the new item actually behaves (asserted vs. imposed) rather than appending it to the list.

evidence: Flag false positive: scoreRun's 'effort: meta.effort' and aggregateRuns's assignment predate review and ff57017 did not touch score.js. The gap was real — the a1318db fix found aggregateRuns' fixture had no effort key so assertions passed vacuously.
guidance_note: When a field is copied from provenance into an artifact, add one test asserting it arrives unchanged at the artifact boundary, not only tests of the downstream consumers with hand-built fixtures.

evidence: The F1 fix added a new exit-2 cause (arm mismatch) but the README's exit-code trichotomy still listed only matcher/N/engine; a1318db adds effort-arm. Reply-hint says already_fixed but the thread shows a plan then 'Fixed in a1318db'.
guidance_note: When the F3-class fix updated three README enumerations, grep for every other enumeration in that file the change outdated (exit codes) instead of only the named ones.

evidence: freeze-suite's censusCases counted runs via listRunDirs only, so a resume under a different --sweep-cap mixed arms until score.js refused after spend — the same mixed-arm-resume gap F9's misarmedRuns closed only in compare.js. a1318db moves misarmedRuns to score.js and refuses in freeze-suite main.
guidance_note: When closing a gap in one entry point, list every CLI that writes into the same --out layout and apply the guard to each.

evidence: a1318db's freeze-suite guard sits in main() before credentialInputFor and had only a manual check; the agent concedes 'a manual check is not a regression test' and adds a credential-free CLI test, mutation-checked against removing and reordering the guard.
guidance_note: When a fix's correctness depends on ordering inside main(), ship a CLI-level test that would fail if the guard moved, in the same commit.

evidence: ff57017 wrote 'matcher, and review-effort arm come FROM whichever baseline' into USAGE; the F10 fix in a1318db corrected the header and README but left this twin. Agent: 'Second round running in which I corrected a claim in one place and left its twin standing two lines away'.
guidance_note: When correcting a wrong claim, grep the exact phrase across the file and README before pushing so every copy changes together.

evidence: The F13 fix in a1318db made censusCases parse every meta.json, and censusCases is also the closing census before the report and timing write, so a malformed run discards a spent suite's record. Agent rejected both reviewer cures (bool flag, try/catch) and split arm-reading into a pre-spend-only priorRunArms, admitting its 'one read' justification was wrong.
guidance_note: Before adding a failing read to a shared function, list all its call sites and check whether any runs after spend where a throw loses already-paid work.

evidence: The a1318db test fixture writeRun hardcoded sweepCap: 2 though the same file already imports DEFAULT_SWEEP_CAP; tests spawning the CLI without --sweep-cap would break with an unrelated arm error if the default moved. Fixed in d0cb0fb.
guidance_note: When a test fixture models 'the default', import the default from its owner rather than writing the current literal.

narrative: The effort-arm PR spent five reviewed rounds and hit the round cap. Nearly every finding after round 0 was fallout: each fix closed one enforcement point or one doc enumeration and left a sibling (pre-spend guard, resumed --out, freeze-suite resume, header vs USAGE vs README). Rounds 2 and 4 contained only fix-caused findings; rounds 1 and 3 each carried one pre-existing gap. The agent named the pattern itself in F12 and F15 but kept fixing one site per finding.
guidance_observations: The original PR deferred the gate-side arm check in its body; closing it up front would have removed the F1-F4-F9-F13-F14 chain's root.
Doc and USAGE corrections were applied per-finding; a grep for the corrected phrase across compare.js and README would have collapsed F7, F8, F10, F12, F15 into one commit.
The round cap was reached with d0cb0fb's fixes (F16, F17) unreviewed, so the merged head stood without review.

evidence: The hunk shows the maxTier comment block sitting directly above the newly inserted readSetProjection describe, so it read as that block's documentation. Moved back above describe('maxTier').
guidance_note: When inserting a block between a comment and its subject, check the comment still sits directly above what it describes.

evidence: readFilesFor(scope.files) returns [] under 'changed' and flowed into buildReviewInput's scopeFiles, which also decides ownsBumpedGoMod, so no worker got the assessDependency directive. Agent split assigned vs read files and added a mutation-verified test.
guidance_note: Before changing the value a parameter carries, grep every read of that parameter in the callee; a parameter serving two meanings has to be split first.

evidence: Flag false positive: a64b129 only bumps the version in package.json and dist; the garbled 'one-arm-per---out' help text was in the original PR. 09ab951 rewrites it.
guidance_note: Run the new --help output and read it once before pushing a new flag.

evidence: Flag false positive: a64b129 is a version bump; the readSet parse branch and its missing type-rejection test predate review. 09ab951 adds readSet: 3 and readSet: [] to the malformed list. The law was cited to justify list placement, which it does not govern.
guidance_note: When adding a new field to a parser with a malformed-input test list, add a bad-type case for the new field in the same commit.

evidence: The flagged commit 09ab951 only touched help text and a test; the real cause is the F2 fix (ccbd159), which moved the empty-read fallback from scopeFiles to readFiles while src/effort.js still said 'buildReviewInput's scopeFiles'. Agent: 'fallout from the ownsBumpedGoMod split'.
guidance_note: When splitting or renaming a parameter, grep comments in other modules for the old name in the same commit.

narrative: A clean read-set axis PR. Round 0 found a real dual-meaning parameter bug (F2) and a displaced comment. Round 1's two ON-POST-REVIEW flags are false positives on a version-bump commit; both were pre-existing small gaps. Round 2's only finding was a stale comment in effort.js left by the F2 parameter split, so that round was avoidable.
guidance_observations: The F2 fix renamed which parameter drives the fallback but did not grep other modules' comments for the old name, costing one round.
